title: NFC Tag Supplier — Stickers, Inlays & Epoxy Tags from Proud Tek
summary: Proud Tek is a Shenzhen NFC tag factory — direct since 2008 and shipping to B2B buyers worldwide — that stocks, prints and encodes NFC tags in every form factor a project actually needs: paper and PET stickers, wet and dry inlays on converter rolls, epoxy tokens, anti-metal tags and tamper-evident labels, all built on 13.56 MHz NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Ultralight and ICODE chips. 'Supplier' here means more than a price list and a shrug: we help you pick the chip, pre-encode the NDEF or SUN record, read-verify every unit, and ship it with the compliance paperwork your buyers will ask for. Below is the chip-and-form-factor menu, the sample-to-PO path, and the certifications a procurement team can check before the first order.
heroPoints: Full NFC form-factor range — NTAG 213 stickers, wet and dry inlays on rolls, epoxy key tags, anti-metal tags and NTAG 424 DNA tamper-evident labels — made and encoded in-house under one ISO 9001 quality system.

Encoding is part of the build, not an afterthought: NDEF URLs, vCards and Wi-Fi records written on the line, NTAG 424 DNA SUN authentication configured to your backend, and every unit read-verified before it ships.

Converter- and reseller-friendly supply — bulk inlay rolls in standard pitches, sample-first ordering, and ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 certificates (98026Q00274R000, 98026E00200R000, 98026S00203R000) you can confirm with the registrar before you talk to us.

sections.title: What a real NFC tag supplier ships
sections.intro: 'NFC tag supplier' covers everyone from a factory to a reseller forwarding your PO to a factory — so the useful question is what actually lands on your dock. Proud Tek makes and encodes the tags in-house: we select the 13.56 MHz chip, build the sticker, inlay or hard tag, write your data, and read-verify each unit before it ships with its [certifications](/about/certifications/) and test records attached. Start with a [free NFC sample pack](/sample-pack/), or jump to the parts most buyers order — [NTAG 213 NFC stickers](/products/rfid-labels/ntag213-nfc-sticker/). The numbers below are the ones a procurement team checks first.
bullets: Form-factor breadth from one line — paper and PET stickers, wet and dry inlays on rolls, epoxy tokens, anti-metal tags and tamper-evident labels — so you consolidate an NFC program with one supplier instead of five.

Direct chip allocation — we run NTAG 213/215/216, NTAG 424 DNA, MIFARE Ultralight and ICODE SLIX2 sourced from NXP and NXP-authorised distribution, so you get genuine silicon with a traceable originality signature, not remarked parts.

Encoding and data services on the line — NDEF URL, vCard, Wi-Fi and app-launch records, plus NTAG 424 DNA SUN (Secure Unique NFC) authentication configured to your server, all 100% read-verified before packing.

Converter- and integrator-ready output — inlays delivered on rolls in standard pitches, tags supplied bare for lamination, and print-and-encode stickers finished to your artwork in standard sizes from a 25 mm round inlay up.
Compliance handled, not hand-waved — RoHS and REACH SVHC material declarations and a Certificate of Conformity per shipment, with quality records retained seven years under ISO 9001.

sections.title: The NFC chip and form-factor menu
sections.intro: This table is the fast way to see whether we cover your part. Everything here runs at 13.56 MHz to a published air-interface standard — ISO/IEC 14443 for NTAG and NTAG 424 DNA, ISO/IEC 15693 for ICODE — so a tag encoded today keeps reading across a phone or reader fleet's lifetime. Chip names are representative of what we stock; browse live parts on the [NFC labels catalogue](/products/rfid-labels/) and [NFC wet inlays](/products/rfid-labels/nfc-wet-inlay/).

rows: Product labels, marketing taps, review prompts

bullets: NTAG 213 — 144 bytes user memory, NFC Forum Type 2 tag, ideal for URL encoding, product authentication and marketing stickers where cost efficiency matters.
NTAG 215 — 504 bytes user memory, commonly used for gaming NFC (Amiibo compatible), loyalty programs and applications needing more data storage.
NTAG 216 — 888 bytes user memory, the largest NTAG chip for vCard storage, complex NDEF records and multi-record applications.

NTAG 424 DNA — AES-128 mutual authentication with a SUN (Secure Unique NFC) message that generates a fresh cryptographic code on every tap, for anti-counterfeit and cloud-verified product authentication (NFC Forum Type 4).
MIFARE Ultralight EV1 — up to 128 bytes user memory with an originality signature and one-time-programmable counters, for single-use tickets, transit fares and event access.
ICODE SLIX2 — an ISO/IEC 15693 vicinity chip at 13.56 MHz built for longer HF read range in library media and industrial-automation tagging.

sections.title: Where a catalogue NFC reseller stops — and where a factory starts
sections.intro: An NFC program goes sideways in the gap between the datasheet and the tag that actually shows up. A trading desk forwards your order and hopes; a factory owns the chip choice, the encoding and the read-test. When your tags carry a brand's reputation — a [tamper-evident NTAG 424 DNA label](/products/rfid-labels/ntag424-dna-tamper-evident-tag/) or an [NFC brand-authentication](/solutions/nfc-brand-authentication/) rollout — that difference is the whole ballgame.

sections.title: From free NFC sample to standing PO
sections.intro: Nobody should buy 50,000 NFC tags they have not tapped. The path below front-loads the cheap, reversible steps — a [free sample pack](/sample-pack/) first, a small paid pilot second, and a locked-price production run only once the parts read cleanly on your own phones and readers.

image.alt: A five-step NFC sourcing flow, left to right. Step 1, free NFC samples: 5-10 encoded tags in 5-10 days. Step 2, spec and quote: chip, size and encoding confirmed in writing. Step 3, pilot run: a 100-piece batch read on your own phone. Step 4, first article and lock: artwork and encoding locked on the traveler. Step 5, volume PO: locked-price run, 100% read-verified. A base arrow shows buyer commitment rising only as risk falls — nothing commits volume until the tags read on your own phone or reader.

items.label: 1. Free NFC samples
items.text: Tell us the application and target chip; we ship 5-10 encoded samples — a sticker, an inlay and a hard tag — so your team can tap them on the actual phones and readers they will meet in the field.

items.label: 2. Spec & quote
items.text: We confirm the chip, form factor, antenna size and encoding scheme (NDEF or SUN) in writing, then quote MOQ, price and lead time — nothing is left implicit before tooling.

items.label: 3. Pilot run
items.text: A 100-piece pilot (or a short inlay roll) encoded with your real data and returned so you can validate read range and phone behaviour side by side before committing volume.

items.label: 4. First article & lock
items.text: The approved sample becomes the reference: chip, antenna, artwork and encoding scheme are locked on the production traveler so unit 1 and unit 50,000 are identical.

items.label: 5. Volume PO
items.text: Full run at locked pricing with 100% read-back verification and the encoding log delivered with the shipment; reorders quote from the same locked spec.

Everything below is verifiable before you commit — the [certifications page](/about/certifications/) shows each standard and how to confirm it with the registrar, and the [factory page](/about/factory/) documents the plant behind the tags.
checklist: ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certificates — certificate number and issuing registrar provided on request for independent verification.
Genuine-silicon proof: NTAG and ICODE parts carry an NXP originality signature you can verify on your own reader, so the chip in the tag is the chip on the quote.
100% read-back verification on every encoded tag, with the NDEF / SUN encoding log delivered alongside the shipment.
Per-shipment documentation pack — Certificate of Conformity plus RoHS and REACH SVHC material declarations by SKU.
Open factory audits at our Shenzhen operation by appointment, with virtual walk-throughs and third-party (SGS, TUV, Intertek) inspection accommodated when a program requires it.
Quality records — encoding logs, read-test data and production travelers — retained seven years under ISO 9001, traceable by SKU or encoding lot.

faq.question: What is the minimum order for NFC tags, and can I test first?
faq.answer: Free samples come first: we ship 5-10 encoded NFC tags of any type so you can tap them before you buy. For production, printed NFC stickers start around 500 pieces, wet or dry inlay rolls around 1,000 pieces, and epoxy or hard tags around 200 pieces — but the exact minimum depends on chip, size and encoding, so we quote it per program rather than post one number that would be wrong for half of them. Send your spec and target volume for written MOQ and pricing.

faq.question: Can you supply NFC tags pre-encoded with our URLs?
faq.answer: Yes — encoding is part of the build. We write NDEF records (static or UID-personalised URLs, vCards, Wi-Fi credentials, app-launch records) on the production line and read-verify every tag. For NTAG 424 DNA we configure the SUN mirror and your backend URL so each tap produces a fresh cryptographic signature for authentication.

faq.question: Do you supply NFC inlays on rolls to label converters?
faq.answer: Yes. Wet inlays ship on continuous rolls with standard pitch spacing (16 mm, 18 mm or custom) compatible with major converting lines from Mühlbauer, Melzer and BIELOMATIK, in narrow-web (50-80 mm) and wide-web (200-320 mm) widths. Tell us your converting equipment and we match the pitch and web width to it.

faq.question: How do I verify your factory and quality before ordering?
faq.answer: Three independent checks. Request our ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certificate numbers and confirm them with the issuing registrar; book a factory audit (in person or virtual) at our Shenzhen operation; and order a sample pack to read the tags on your own phones and equipment. Every claim on this page is meant to be checked, not taken on faith.

faq.question: How do I choose between NTAG 213, 215, 216 and NTAG 424 DNA?
faq.answer: Match memory and security to the job. NTAG 213 is the cost-efficient default for a URL or review link on a sticker; NTAG 215 and NTAG 216 add user memory for vCards, multi-record NDEF or app data; NTAG 424 DNA adds AES-128 SUN authentication for when a tag has to prove it is genuine, as in brand protection. Not sure? A mixed sample pack lets you tap all four and decide on the evidence.
